# Link

Link: an inline navigation anchor.

**Import:** `import { Link } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.stories.jsx` — Appearances, OpenInNewWindow, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations · Motion.

## Usage

Use `Link` for navigation inside a sentence or a block of text — "see the
session report," "read more." For a standalone action styled like a button,
use `Button` or `LinkButton` instead; `Link`'s appearances are for text, not
for a control that stands on its own.

## Best practices

### Pick the appearance for the surface it sits on, not for emphasis. {#pick-the-appearance-for-the-surface-it-sits-on-not-for-emphasis}

`default` is for a link on the page's own background, `subtle` for one on a
muted surface where less contrast reads better, and `inverse` for a link on a
dark or colored fill. None of the three changes the link's meaning.

### Make the link text name the destination. {#make-the-link-text-name-the-destination}

Do: The words say where the link goes.
Don't: Link text that means nothing out of context.

### Let `isOpenInNewWindow` manage `target` and `rel` together. {#let-isopeninnewwindow-manage-target-and-rel-together}

Setting `isOpenInNewWindow` adds the external-link glyph, appends spoken text to the accessible name, and defaults `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Pass `target` or `rel` directly only when the default pairing does not fit.

Do: The glyph and the spoken warning come with the prop.
Don't: Warning typed into the text: the glyph is missing and it reads twice.

### Keep the link inside the sentence it finishes. {#keep-the-link-inside-the-sentence-it-finishes}

A link is inline text. When the action stands alone, such as Save or Continue, it is a button, not a link.

Do: The link sits on the words that name the destination.
Don't: A standalone action dressed as a link. Use a button.

## Accessibility

- **A real anchor.** `Link` renders an `<a>`, reachable with Tab and
  activated with Enter, with no extra role needed.
- **New-window links say so.** The glyph is decorative, but the accessible
  name gains "(opens in a new tab)" through visually hidden text, so a screen
  reader announces the behavior before it happens.
- **`children` is required.** A link always needs visible or accessible text
  — there is no icon-only mode.

## Related

- For a standalone action styled like a button, use `LinkButton`.
- For a trail of links showing where a page sits, use `Breadcrumb`.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Pagination` · `Sidebar` · `Tabs`

## Parts

1. **Text.** The link's name, in the appearance's ink.
2. **Underline.** Always on for `default` and `inverse`; `subtle` shows it on hover.
3. **New-window glyph.** Added by `isOpenInNewWindow`, with “(opens in a new tab)” appended to the accessible name.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Default in the link ink, underlined; visited in the visited ink. |
| Hovered | Subtle is underlined; default keeps its ink. |
| Pressed | The pressed link ink on default and subtle. |
| Focused | The 2px ring, 2px off the link; the inverse ring on a dark fill. |
| Disabled | Not a state. A link with nowhere to go is plain text, not a dimmed link. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Default | `--ds-link`, `--ds-link-visited`, `--ds-link-pressed` |
| Subtle | `--ds-text`, `--ds-link-pressed` |
| Inverse | `--ds-text-inverse`, ring `--ds-border-focused-inverse` |
| Corners | `--radius-lg` |
| New-window glyph | `--icon-sm`, `--inline-md` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Make the text say where it goes: “View the full report”. | Use “click here” or “read more”. |
| Put the link on the words that name the destination. | Stretch it over a whole sentence. |
| Write it in sentence case, without ending punctuation inside the link. | Add an arrow or “>” to the text; the glyph does that job. |
| Warn about a new window with `isOpenInNewWindow`. | Say “(opens in new tab)” in the text yourself. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `href` | string (required) | — | The destination URL of the anchor. Required. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | `default` for links in body text; `subtle` for links inside secondary or quiet text; `inverse` for links on dark or colored grounds. |
| `target` | string | — | Pass-through to the anchor; `isOpenInNewWindow` sets `_blank` when neither is given. |
| `rel` | string | — | The anchor `rel` attribute. Defaults to `noopener noreferrer` when the link opens in a new tab. |
| `isOpenInNewWindow` | bool | `false` | Draws the new-window glyph and appends it to the accessible name. Also defaults `target` to `_blank`. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the anchor beside the component's own. |
| `children` | node (required) | — | The link text. Required, since it names the link. |
